# bitfab-lib

Leaf modules shared between `bitfab-web` and the editor plugins.

| Subpath | Owns | Consumers |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `bitfab-lib/mcp-contract` | name, title, description and input schema for the shared MCP tool surface | `bitfab-web/src/app/mcp/route.ts`, `bitfab-plugin-lib/src/mcpServer.ts` |
| `bitfab-lib/frameworks` | which frameworks' auto-captured model span runs through `withSpan` | `bitfab-plugin-lib/src/flows/frameworks.ts` |

This package exists because both MCP servers previously defined the same tool surface by hand, behind
five "keep in sync" comments, and had already drifted on `get_span_field.maxChars`.

## Packaging rules

Unlike every other workspace package, this one is bundled into **bitfab-web's serverless runtime**.
Three rules follow. Each was learned by breaking something.

**1. Subpath exports only. Never add a `"."` export or a root barrel.**

`bitfab-plugin-lib` cannot be imported into a Next server build: its barrel re-exports 82 modules and
one of them does a dynamic import Turbopack cannot statically resolve. A root barrel here would
invite the same failure, so there isn't one. Add a new subpath per module instead.

**2. `files: ["dist"]` in package.json is load-bearing. Do not remove it.**

`dist/` is gitignored and there is no `main` field, so nothing implicitly pulls the build output into
the packed package. Without `files`, `pnpm deploy` vendors the plugin with `src/` and `package.json`
but no compiled JS, and the plugin's MCP server dies at import with `ERR_MODULE_NOT_FOUND`. Every
typecheck, unit test and `next build` still passes: only a real stdio run against the vendored plugin
catches it.

**3. Nothing reachable from a subpath may import a node builtin or use a dynamic import.**

Multi-module packages and relative `./x.js` specifiers are fine (verified against a real
`next build`). Node builtins and dynamic imports are what break the bundle. Anything needing those
belongs in `bitfab-plugin-lib`, which is plugin-only.

## Adding a module

1. Add `src/<name>.ts` (zod is the only permitted dependency).
2. Add a `./<name>` entry to `exports` pointing at `dist/<name>.js` and `dist/<name>.d.ts`.
3. Add `bitfab-lib/**` coverage where needed in `.github/change-gate.json` (already present for all
   current consumers).

`bitfab-lib` is already wired into `scripts/build-bitfab-internal.sh` (built before
`bitfab-plugin-lib`, and hashed in the deploy-skip check), `scripts/vendor-bitfab-plugin.sh`, and
`scripts/check-version-bump.sh` (a change here requires a plugin version bump, because it ships
inside every plugin).

## Enum parity

The contract hardcodes wire enums because it may not import bitfab-web's `db/` or `domains/`.
`bitfab-web/src/app/mcp/mcpContractParity.test.ts` asserts each one still matches the database enum,
so adding a grader model, span type, span field or confidence level on one side fails there.
`bitfab-plugin-lib/src/flows/frameworks.test.ts` does the same for `frameworks`.
